_comment: Edit this file after training and evaluating a model. See docs/AI_MODEL_GUIDE.md. Never enter results you did not measure.
source: Trained by the project with the Teachable Machine library (same method as the Teachable Machine website) from openly licensed public datasets. See docs/MODEL_EVALUATION.md.
architecture: Two Teachable Machine image models (MobileNet v2 transfer learning) run in the browser with TensorFlow.js: a fruit recogniser (fruit names + "Not a fruit") and a freshness checker (fruit × Fresh/Spoiled + "Other"). The app only shows a freshness answer when both agree.
trainingData: Sultana et al. 2022 (CC BY 4.0), FruitNet (CC BY 4.0), Papaya Freshness Dataset (CC BY 4.0), FruQ-DB/FruQ-multi (CC BY 4.0), FruitVision (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, mango + some grapes), Fruits-360 (CC BY-SA 4.0, fruit recogniser). Up to 500 fresh + 500 spoiled photos per freshness fruit. Full list: data/v2/images.csv (local).
testProcedure: Thresholds chosen on validation photos; final results on 2736 freshness test photos and 4963 recogniser test photos never used for training. Near-identical photos and neighbouring video frames were kept on one side of the split.
thresholdNote: Freshness threshold chosen on 2026-10-18 from 1331 validation photos; recogniser threshold 70.0% chosen from 2504 validation photos (lowest with ≥95% correct when answered). Dataset photos only — re-check with your own phone photos.

knownLimitations: The models look only at the outside of the fruit in one photo. They cannot see inside the fruit, detect bacteria or toxins, or decide whether food is safe to eat.
Whole-image classifiers: they do not point to particular spots, mould patches or defects.
Trained and tested only on public dataset photos. Accuracy on your own phone photos is likely lower and has not been measured yet.
Freshness is checked only for fruits with licensed fresh/rotten photos; other fruits are only named.
Many recogniser photos (Fruits-360) show single fruits rotating on a white background, so recognition of those fruits in real kitchens may be weaker.
No "overripe" class: the datasets label fresh and rotten only.
Everyday objects that are not fruit can still be mistaken for a fruit.
